newsitem.title: USA: Urologix behind plan for T3 application.
newsitem.headline: Urologix behind plan for T3 application.

text.p: Urologix Inc said on Wednesday that it is 30 to 60 days behind its plan to apply to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for pre-market approval of its treatment of prostate disease.

"We continue to be very encouraged with the clinical data being collected from our studies. However, data compilation, to support our PMA (pre-market approval) submission, is 30 to 60 days behind our original plan," said Jack Meyer, Urologix president, in a statement. "While we are working hard to get back on schedule, we now expect to submit our PMA application to the FDA in the first calendar quarter of 1997," he said.
During its fiscal 1997 first quarter ended September 30, 1996, Urologix said it generated the first revenue from its T3 Targeted Transurethral Thermo-ablation System in Europe.
The product received European marketing approval in early July.
The T3 System is designed to treat enlarged prostate, a disease affecting over 23 million men worldwide.

In reporting its first sales, Meyer said: "This achievement represents an important milestone for Urologix, as well as evidence of significant progress in our transition from a development-stage company to a commercial business."
